also: passing from one stage to another

terms.gloss: a passing over; a change from one state or stage to another
evidence: Quint. 11.3.28: in illō ā pueritiā ad adulēscentiam trānsitū (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The going across, literally (a ditch, a river: Cic. Tusc. 5.59) and of any change of state, party or stage; Pliny uses it of the shading of one colour into another (Plin. NH 35.29).

terms.gloss: a going over; in a speech, the passage from one part to the next
terms.comment: Classically chiefly a going over to the other side, a desertion (Liv. 28.15.14); the rhetorical sense is the transition between sections.
The general word for a change; trānsitus adds the passage from one point to the next.

sources: Lewis & Short: transitus · Lewis & Short: transitio · Lewis & Short: mutatio
